slot.brief: Force given as a function of position along a straight line; find work done in moving from one coordinate to another by integration.

stem: A particle moving along the $x$-axis is acted upon by a force $F = (3x^2 - 2x + 4)\ \text{N}$, where $x$ is in metres. The work done by this force in displacing the particle from $x = 1\ \text{m}$ to $x = 3\ \text{m}$ is
working:
The work done by a variable force along a straight line is given by:
$$W = \int_{x_i}^{x_f} F(x)\,dx$$

Substituting the given force function and limits:
$$W = \int_{1}^{3} (3x^2 - 2x + 4)\,dx$$

Evaluating the definite integral:
$$W = \left[ x^3 - x^2 + 4x \right]_{1}^{3}$$

At the upper limit ($x = 3\ \text{m}$):
$$(3)^3 - (3)^2 + 4(3) = 27 - 9 + 12 = 30\ \text{J}$$

At the lower limit ($x = 1\ \text{m}$):
$$(1)^3 - (1)^2 + 4(1) = 1 - 1 + 4 = 4\ \text{J}$$

Subtracting the lower limit from the upper limit:
$$W = 30 - 4 = 26\ \text{J}$$

Independent check: W = ∫₁³ (3x²−2x+4) dx = [x³−x²+4x]₁³ = (27−9+12) − (1−1+4) = 30−4 = 26 J.

draft.distractor_notes:
$18\ \text{J}$: Forgetting to divide by 2 when integrating $2x$, using $\int 2x\,dx = 2x^2$, giving $(21 - 3) = 18\ \text{J}$.
$30\ \text{J}$: Evaluating only at the upper limit ($x = 3\ \text{m}$) and neglecting the lower limit.
$34\ \text{J}$: Adding the lower-limit value instead of subtracting it ($30 + 4 = 34\ \text{J}$).
